merge.subject: feat: decide what custody claims, and mechanise what can be checked (#23)
merge.body:
Resolves #23. §5's mechanical check did not work — agents in worktrees inherit the researcher's git identity, so git log --format='%an' -- CONTEXT.md returned NGL321 either way. Custody was a norm wearing a mechanism's clothes, which is precisely the unverifiable authorship claim §5 exists to prevent.

Prototyped on prototype/custody-predicate — the ticket's three readings plus two more as pure predicates, driven by hand against this repository's real CONTEXT.md history. That branch is working scratch, not a source of record. §4 puts prototype/ in the "dies on merge" class, so nothing load-bearing may live there; what the exercise settled is argued in this description and in §5 itself, both of which land on main. The branch is worth reading while it exists, and nothing depends on it existing.

Bump: tooling MINOR
